sanskrit_verse: धर्मोपदेशकर्ता च वेदोदाहरणान्वितः । आक्रोशकस्तु विप्राणां जिह्वाच्छेदेन दण्ड्यते ॥
transliteration: dharmopadeśakartā ca vedodāharaṇānvitaḥ | ākrośakastu viprāṇāṃ jihvācchedena daṇḍyate ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who teaches Dharma and cites the Vedas is honored; but one who reviles the twice-born shall have his tongue severed.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derives from alignment with Vedic truth and Dharma-teaching capacity.
Causation arises from speech that disrupts sacred order versus speech that upholds it.
Capacity-based responsibility distinguishes between reverent teaching and defiling utterance.
Restoration logic mandates removal of capacity to cause further violation through speech.
Consciousness alignment requires protection of sacred knowledge channels.
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent utters defamatory speech against a twice-born THEN disable vocal instrument permanently.
IF agent teaches Dharma citing Vedas THEN grant societal recognition and support.
IF speech act violates sacred ontological categories THEN automatic irreversible incapacitation occurs without punitive intent.
IF individual demonstrates alignment with Vedic-Dharmic order THEN elevate social status automatically.
supreme_court_application: Supreme judicial authority recognizes inherent ontological consequences in speech acts. Defiling a twice-born constitutes structural damage to cosmic order; hence, natural incapacitation occurs at the level of bodily function, not external punishment. Courts affirm pre-existing Dharma-law rather than impose judgment.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes clear causal link between reviling sacred beings and loss of speech capacity. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as immediate consequence within consciousness-field. Responsibility aligns with volition behind harmful speech. No suffering is induced; natural consequence restores balance.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process ensures cessation of disruptive speech pattern.
Responsibility assumption by community to protect sacred persons.
Capacity restoration through ritual purification for collective awareness upliftment.
Integrity reintegration via public affirmation of Vedic-teaching value.
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands executed: consciousness itself enforces Dharma. There is no punishment—only inevitable consequence. The tongue severs not by hand, but by reality's own alignment with sacred order. Thus Dharma is restored, reality remains non-punitive, and consciousness reigns as sole adjudicator.
